meta.description: Test read. A multi-line free-text field with a label, a helper message and a character counter. Read independently of the existing Text Area page to measure whether the framework reproduces its own result.

verdict.title: Fix — the error state and the disabled value colour
verdict.text: Two axes, a complete 8-variant matrix and three text layers all bound to DS styles. But error changes only the border, and a disabled field renders real content at the placeholder colour — so content and emptiness look the same.

overview.inContextNote: A comment or message box inside a form — a label above, the field, and a helper line carrying both the hint and the character count. Sketched; no screenshot of a shipping screen was read in this pass.
overview.inContextAlt: A form screen with a labelled multi-line text field, helper text at the lower left and a character counter at the lower right, above a submit button.

traits.name: Reusable
traits.note: Any free-text input that needs more than one line and a length limit. Nothing in the set is bound to one product, and the label, helper and counter are all content rather than baked copy.

traits.name: Self-contained
traits.note: It owns its schema and every part it draws: the header, the field box and the helper line are all inside the component, and it depends on nothing above it in the tree.

traits.name: Consistent
traits.note: Three of the four states behave alike — white surface, coloured border, navy value when filled. Disabled breaks all three: no border at all, a tinted surface, and a filled value left at the placeholder colour. Error is the only state whose meaning is not carried anywhere but the border.

traits.name: Composable
traits.note: The header and the helper line are real instances (FormGroup Header, Subtext Message), but the field box between them is a plain FRAME redrawn inside all eight variants. Half the component composes, half is drawn in place.

behavior.notes: Resting field. Surface #FFFFFF, border #D7E0EF at 1, placeholder #90A8D0.
Border turns #005CE5 and thickens to 2. Surface, value and helper are unchanged.
Border turns #D61B2C at 2 — and nothing else changes. The helper text stays #6780A9, exactly as in Default.
Surface #EEF2F9 and the border is removed entirely. The helper line does not dim; it stays #6780A9.
The box grows 34 → 50 as the value wraps to two lines and the counter reads 71/100. The value goes #0A2757 in every state but Disabled, where it stays #90A8D0.

open.headline: Error is carried by the border colour alone.
open.body: Between State=Default and State=Error the only difference is the box border: #D7E0EF at 1 becomes #D61B2C at 2. The helper text stays #6780A9 in both, there is no error message, and no icon appears. Colour is the sole carrier of the error, which fails WCAG 2.2 §1.4.1 Use of Color at Level A.

open.headline: A disabled field renders real content at the placeholder colour.
open.body: On State=Disabled, hasValue=True (node 4781:35854) the value is #90A8D0 — the same fill the placeholder uses. Every other state takes a filled value to #0A2757. A disabled field holding real text is therefore the same tone as an empty one, at 2.15:1 against the #EEF2F9 surface.

open.headline: Helper text and placeholder are both below the contrast minimum.
open.body: The helper and counter are #6780A9 on #FFFFFF — 4.01:1, under the 4.5:1 that 12px text needs. The placeholder is #90A8D0 on #FFFFFF — 2.41:1. Both computed from the read fills with the WCAG relative-luminance formula, so both are checkable.

open.headline: Two sibling layers share the name #subtext.
open.body: The Subtext Message instance holds two text nodes, both named #subtext: the helper on the left and the counter on the right. They carry different content and would map to different parameters, but nothing in the layer tree tells them apart.

open.headline: The field box is a local frame, not a component.
open.body: The header and helper line are instances, but the box between them is a plain FRAME named Text Area, drawn again inside each of the eight variants. Any change to the field shape has to be made eight times, and the box cannot be reused by the other field components that need the same treatment.

recommendations.headline: Give the error a second signal.
recommendations.body: Swap the helper line for an error message in the error state, or add a leading icon. The border may stay as reinforcement, but it cannot be the only thing that says "error".

recommendations.headline: Separate the disabled value colour from the placeholder colour.
recommendations.body: A disabled field still shows what the user wrote. Give it its own dimmed value token — dark enough to read, clearly not editable — instead of reusing the placeholder fill.

recommendations.headline: Raise the helper and placeholder to 4.5:1.
recommendations.body: Both sit below the minimum on white. The helper carries the character limit, which is information the user needs before they hit it, so it is not decorative text.

recommendations.headline: Name the helper and the counter apart.
recommendations.body: Two layers called #subtext cannot be mapped to two parameters without guessing which is which. #helper and #counter would carry straight into the API.

recommendations.headline: Make the field box its own component.
recommendations.body: Input Field, Search Field, Select Field and this one all draw the same bordered box. Extracting it once would let all of them compose it, and would stop the eight copies here drifting apart.

recommendations.headline: Say what the counter counts and what happens at the limit.
recommendations.body: The counter reads 0/100 and 71/100, but nothing on the component says whether input is blocked at 100, whether the count is characters or bytes, or whether crossing it sets the error state.

accessibility.ios: Pass the label to EBTextArea so it becomes the accessibilityLabel; never rely on the visual label alone.
accessibility.android: Modifier.semantics { contentDescription = label }, or a TextField label slot so TalkBack reads it before the value.

accessibility.ios: The red border carries nothing to VoiceOver. Set accessibilityValue to the error message and post .announcement when it appears.
accessibility.android: Modifier.semantics { error(errorMessage) } so the state is spoken, not only drawn.

accessibility.ios: Expose the remaining count through accessibilityValue, and announce when the limit is reached rather than silently truncating.
accessibility.android: Put the count in stateDescription and use liveRegion when it crosses the limit.

accessibility.ios: .disabled(true) sets .notEnabled; do not fake it by making the field read-only, or VoiceOver still offers editing.
accessibility.android: enabled = false so the node reports itself disabled instead of merely looking it.

accessibility.requirement: Multi-line growth is not a trap
accessibility.ios: The field grows with content; keep it inside a scroll view so the caret stays visible with the keyboard up.
accessibility.android: Pair with imePadding() and a scrollable parent so the growing field is not hidden behind the IME.

usageGuidelines.doText: Use Text Area when the answer runs past one line — a message, a reason, an address.
usageGuidelines.dontText: Do not use it for a single short value; Input Field is the one-line control and keeps the counter off screen.

usageGuidelines.doText: Set a limit the user can actually reach, and show the counter from the start.
usageGuidelines.dontText: Do not hide the counter until the limit is close — the user has already written past it by then.

usageGuidelines.doText: Write the helper line as the rule the field enforces.
usageGuidelines.dontText: Do not repeat the label in the helper line; it is the only place the limit and format can be explained.

scorecard.notes: The conventions hold — ValueContainer and Value inside the box, #-prefixed text layers, Title Case variant values. Against that: the Subtext Message instance carries two sibling layers both named #subtext, and the field box repeats the component's own name.

Two orthogonal axes, all eight combinations built, Title Case state values and a boolean correctly named hasValue. Boolean, instance-swap and text properties are not readable with this toolchain, so any beyond these two are unverified rather than absent.

Not scorable with this toolchain, but half-answered. Type is fully bound: all three text roles resolve to DS styles — Primary/Label/Light/Small, Primary/Multi-line Label/Light/Small and Secondary/Bold/Caption. Colour cannot be resolved to token names: the file exposes only a Prototype States collection and the DS variables sit in an unenumerable library. Needs a Dev Mode read.

State maps to focus, validation and enabled; hasValue is content rather than a parameter, which is correct. What costs it a Ready: the field box is a local frame rather than a component, so nothing tells a developer that this box is the same box Input Field and Search Field draw.

All four states are built and are visually distinct, but two of them are wrong rather than merely thin. Error changes only the border, so colour is the sole carrier — a Level A failure of WCAG §1.4.1. Disabled renders entered content at the placeholder fill, at 2.15:1. The helper text is 4.01:1 and the placeholder 2.41:1 on white, both under the minimum.
The component draws no icons, images or vectors — a label, a bordered box and two lines of caption text. Nothing to score.

variants.description: 4 State × 2 hasValue = 8 variants — a complete matrix, no gaps and no correlated axes.

rows.body: Independent trial read of Text Area, run against the refined framework. The component already has a page at Text Area; this one was written from a fresh Figma read without consulting it, so the two can be compared. It stays out of the sidebar, search, the grid and the counts.

All 8 variants were read off set 4781:35856, and the whole set plus three box frames were exported — the frames as SVG, which is how the border weights below were read (Default 1, Focused and Error 2, Disabled none). get_node_info does not return stroke weight.
The three contrast ratios are computed from the read fills with the WCAG 2.2 relative-luminance formula, not read from Figma. The inputs are printed beside them so each one can be checked.

Padding, gap and alignment are reported unread: the Talk To Figma plugin returns no auto-layout fields and the Dev Mode toolchain was not authorised in this session. They are left blank rather than derived from bounding boxes.
